title: Merge measurements and make a report
intro: Join source metadata and microscope-field measurements without multiplying rows, summarize explicitly, reshape safely, preserve timestamps, export traceable CSVs and actual Matplotlib plots. Inference/uncertainty is reserved for I12.

scientific_context.caution: Synthetic field data and plotting exercises do not justify a biological effect estimate, replication claim or publication-ready figure.

chapter_method: Predict → Run → Investigate → Apply → Prove, with genuine Pandas and Matplotlib execution and scientific audit.

goals.title: Join imaging data to specimen metadata safely
goals.why: A nonunique specimen table can multiply imaging records during a merge and distort a reported experiment.
explain: Use `pd.merge` with explicit join keys, `how='left'`, and `validate='many_to_one'` when many image fields may belong to a single specimen.
Before merging, inspect whether source metadata contain duplicated specimen IDs. Reject an ambiguous source rather than silently multiplying rows.
Unmatched image fields must be reported with their original IDs. A successful join cannot independently validate biological specimen identity.

Categorical variables represent experimental conditions, not measurements; preserving original spelling is important for provenance.
A UTC timestamp does not alone establish temporal acquisition order or instrument-clock synchronization.

Accessible design requires labels and marker distinctions, not color as the only encoded property; avoid claiming publication readiness without reviewer-level audit.

explain: Matplotlib's `fig.savefig` can produce SVG vector graphics or PNG raster data. Record the target format, resolution and source as part of report provenance.
A large PNG byte stream proves file generation, not correct scientific interpretation. Browser output may be embedded but local use should preserve the original source image and script.
Do not call a figure publication-ready solely because it is 300 DPI; annotations, statistics, accessibility and data validity require independent review.

worked_example.predict: What output would the data produce, and what scientific conclusion does it not justify?

goals.prediction_answer: The output follows actual source rows or plotting objects. Source validity and biological replication need separate evidence.
walkthrough: Check column names and whether keys can appear once or multiple times.
Predict the result and run real Pandas or Matplotlib with changed inputs.
Explain the origin of the experimental unit and which inference is unsupported.
investigate: Try missing rows, changed keys or an invalid metadata join.
Preserve source IDs and record the exact descriptive output.
Test whether plot axes or file exports maintain stated units and provenance.
goals.debug_task: Find an unsafe assumption in export reproducible vector and raster figures and demonstrate it with a new input.
goals.misconception: A merged table or attractive figure proves data are independent biological replicates or publication-ready.
goals.scientific_boundary: All field and specimen measurements are synthetic training data. Display plots and grouped field means are descriptive only, never evidence of statistical significance.

capstone.title: Build a joined and traceable microscopy reporting workflow
capstone.why: A valid report must retain identities, avoid join-driven row multiplication, keep missing data visible and create a clear figure without pretending to perform biological inference.
explain: Start from field-level synthetic measurement rows and specimen metadata; validate uniqueness of sample keys before joining.
Preserve every field row, report unmatched specimen IDs and explicit missing values, and generate descriptive per-sample summaries.
Create an actual Matplotlib display of descriptive values with units, while avoiding statistical claims based on fields or an unverified biological unit.

# I08-CAPSTONE | LEARN | Build a joined and traceable microscopy reporting workflow
# TASK: Predict, run and change the data in the example.

import pandas as pd
fields=pd.DataFrame({'sample_id':['A','A'],'field_id':['F1','F2'],'value':[1,2]})
meta=pd.DataFrame({'sample_id':['A'],'condition':['ctrl']})
print(fields.merge(meta,on='sample_id',validate='many_to_one').shape)
